questions.text: The paradox of thrift suggests that if everyone simultaneously attempts to save more during a recession
questions.explanation: If everyone reduces consumption to save more, aggregate demand can fall, causing lower output and income, which may make total saving fail to increase as expected.

questions.text: Which of the following is an automatic stabilizer
options: A new road construction programme requiring parliamentary approval
A deliberate increase in government borrowing
questions.explanation: Progressive taxation automatically reduces disposable income during booms and eases the tax burden during downturns, helping to stabilize economic activity.

questions.text: If the government reduces taxes during a recession, the most immediate objective is to
options: increase household disposable income and aggregate demand
questions.explanation: Lower taxes increase disposable income, potentially raising consumption and aggregate demand.

questions.text: A government may finance a budget deficit by issuing bonds. The major concern with persistent borrowing is that
options: government revenue will automatically become zero
questions.explanation: Persistent borrowing increases public debt and future debt-service obligations, potentially becoming unsustainable.

questions.text: If the central bank raises interest rates sharply, which of the following is most likely in the short run
questions.explanation: Higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive, discouraging some consumer spending and private investment.

questions.text: A government wants to reduce inflation caused primarily by excessive aggregate demand without significantly reducing productive capacity. Which combination is most appropriate
options: Increase money supply and reduce taxes
Reduce excessive government spending and tighten monetary conditions
Increase subsidies and reduce interest rates
Increase government consumption and reduce taxes
questions.explanation: Both tighter fiscal and monetary policies can reduce excess aggregate demand, helping to control demand-pull inflation.

questions.text: A consumer has an income of ₦24,000 and can buy either commodity X at ₦2,000 per unit or commodity Y at ₦3,000 per unit. If the consumer spends all income on X, the opportunity cost of purchasing one unit of X in terms of Y is
questions.explanation: One unit of X costs ₦2,000, while one unit of Y costs ₦3,000. Therefore, ₦2,000 represents 2/3 of a unit of Y. The opportunity cost of one unit of X is 2/3 unit of Y.

questions.text: An economy produces only food and machinery. If producing 100 additional units of machinery requires sacrificing 400 units of food, the opportunity cost of one unit of machinery is
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost = 400 ÷ 100 = 4 units of food per machinery unit.

questions.text: A country's production possibility curve is bowed outward from the origin. This shape primarily reflects
questions.explanation: A bowed-out PPC reflects increasing opportunity cost because resources are not equally efficient in producing different goods.

questions.text: If the government introduces a subsidy on the production of a commodity, assuming other factors remain constant, the most likely immediate effect is
options: a movement along the demand curve only
questions.explanation: A subsidy reduces producers' effective production costs, encouraging supply and shifting the supply curve rightward.

questions.text: Suppose the equilibrium price of a commodity is ₦800. The government fixes a maximum price of ₦600. Which of the following is most likely to occur
questions.explanation: A binding price ceiling below equilibrium causes quantity demanded to exceed quantity supplied, creating a shortage.

questions.text: A farmer's total revenue rises from ₦1,000,000 to ₦1,100,000 following a 20% increase in the price of his product. Assuming quantity changes accordingly, demand for the product is
questions.explanation: Price rises by 20%, while total revenue rises only 10%. With an inelastic demand, a price increase increases total revenue.

questions.text: If the price of a commodity increases by 10% and quantity demanded falls by 30%, the price elasticity of demand is
questions.explanation: PED = 30% ÷ 10% = 3. Demand is therefore elastic.

questions.text: A firm's total revenue is ₦1,500,000 when it sells 30,000 units. If its total cost is ₦1,200,000, its average profit per unit is
A firm has fixed costs of ₦200,000 and variable costs of ₦500,000 at an output of 10,000 units. Its average total cost is
When marginal cost is below average cost, average cost will
questions.explanation: MC pulls the average toward itself. If MC is below AC, it causes average cost to fall.

questions.text: A firm experiences diseconomies of scale when
options: long-run average cost falls as output rises
long-run average cost rises as output rises
output increases more than proportionately to inputs
questions.explanation: Diseconomies of scale occur when expansion causes long-run average cost to increase.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to cause diseconomies of scale in a very large firm
questions.explanation: Very large organizations may experience management, communication and coordination problems, causing average costs to rise.

questions.text: A perfectly competitive industry is characterized by all of the following EXCEPT
options: significant control over market price by individual firms
questions.explanation: Individual firms in perfect competition are price takers, not price makers.

questions.text: If a perfectly competitive firm increases its price above the market price, its sales will most likely
questions.explanation: Since identical products are available from other sellers at the market price, consumers will buy elsewhere. The individual firm faces perfectly elastic demand.

questions.text: A monopolist can practise price discrimination when
options: all consumers have identical demand conditions
resale between markets is impossible or difficult
the firm has no control over price
questions.explanation: Price discrimination requires the seller to separate markets and prevent consumers from buying cheaply in one market and reselling in another.

questions.text: A monopolist charges ₦1,000 in Market A and ₦1,500 in Market B for the same product. This can be sustained only if
options: consumers can freely resell between markets
the two markets can be effectively separated
demand is identical in both markets
the firm has no market power
questions.explanation: Effective market separation prevents arbitrage and allows the monopolist to charge different prices.

questions.text: The kinked-demand curve model is particularly associated with
questions.explanation: The kinked-demand model explains price rigidity and strategic interdependence in oligopolistic markets.

questions.text: A major reason firms in an oligopoly may avoid frequent price changes is that
options: consumers do not respond to prices
questions.explanation: Because firms are mutually interdependent, a price change may trigger reactions from competitors.

questions.text: If a country's working population is 20 million and 2 million are unemployed, the unemployment rate is
questions.explanation: Unemployment rate = 2m ÷ 20m × 100 = 10%.

questions.text: A graduate who refuses available jobs because the offered wages are below his preferred level is best classified as
questions.explanation: Voluntary unemployment occurs when a person chooses not to accept available employment, often because of wage or job preferences.

questions.text: A worker loses his job because the skills required by employers have changed due to technological advancement. This is
questions.explanation: Structural unemployment occurs when there is a mismatch between workers' skills and available jobs.

questions.text: A worker who is temporarily unemployed while moving from one job to another is experiencing
questions.explanation: Frictional unemployment arises during the normal process of searching for or changing jobs.

questions.text: During a recession, firms reduce production and lay off workers. This is most directly associated with
questions.explanation: Cyclical unemployment results from declines in economic activity during business-cycle downturns.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to reduce structural unemployment
questions.explanation: Retraining helps workers acquire the skills demanded by employers, reducing skill mismatch.

questions.text: If nominal wages rise by 5% while the general price level rises by 8%, real wages will approximately
questions.explanation: Approximately, real wage change = nominal wage growth − inflation = 5% − 8% = −3%.

questions.text: A country's national income is ₦50 billion and its population is 5 million. Its per capita income is
questions.explanation: ₦50 billion ÷ 5 million = ₦10,000 per person.

questions.text: If real national income increases from ₦80 billion to ₦92 billion, the growth rate is
Economic growth differs from economic development because economic development
options: concerns only an increase in nominal GDP
includes qualitative improvements in living standards and structural transformation
questions.explanation: Economic growth focuses mainly on increased output, while development includes health, education, living standards, structural change and broader welfare improvements.

questions.text: A country records rapid GDP growth but experiences worsening income inequality, poor healthcare and declining environmental quality. This suggests that
options: GDP growth alone may not adequately measure economic development
questions.explanation: GDP growth does not automatically translate into broad improvements in human welfare and quality of life.

questions.text: The Human Development Index is more comprehensive than per capita income because it considers factors such as
questions.explanation: HDI incorporates dimensions including income, education and life expectancy.

questions.text: If the marginal propensity to consume is 0.75, the simple investment multiplier is
questions.explanation: Multiplier = 1/(1 − MPC) = 1/0.25 = 4.

questions.text: If government investment increases by ₦5 billion and the MPC is 0.8, the maximum increase in equilibrium income, under the simple multiplier model, is
questions.explanation: Multiplier = 1/(1 − 0.8) = 5. Income increase = ₦5bn × 5 = ₦25bn.

questions.text: An economy has a marginal propensity to save of 0.25. Its investment multiplier is
questions.explanation: Multiplier = 1/MPS = 1/0.25 = 4.

questions.text: If consumers' marginal propensity to consume increases, the simple expenditure multiplier will
questions.explanation: A higher MPC means a smaller MPS. Since multiplier = 1/MPS, the multiplier increases.

questions.text: Which of the following is a monetary policy instrument
questions.explanation: Open market operations involve the central bank buying or selling securities to influence money supply and liquidity.

questions.text: If the central bank buys government securities from commercial banks, the immediate effect is likely to be
questions.explanation: Central-bank purchases inject funds into the banking system, increasing commercial-bank reserves and liquidity.

questions.text: Which combination is most likely to be expansionary
options: Higher interest rates and higher taxes
Lower government spending and higher reserve requirements
Lower interest rates and increased government spending
questions.explanation: Lower interest rates encourage borrowing and spending, while increased government spending raises aggregate demand. Both are expansionary measures.

questions.text: A country experiences persistent inflation alongside rapidly rising production costs. Which of the following is the most plausible cause
questions.explanation: Rising wages, fuel prices, imported inputs or other production costs can shift aggregate supply leftward, producing cost-push inflation.

questions.text: If the domestic currency appreciates substantially, holding other factors constant, domestic exports become
questions.explanation: Appreciation increases the foreign-currency price of domestic goods, making exports less competitive internationally.

questions.text: A country imposes a tariff on imported rice mainly to protect domestic rice producers. If the tariff succeeds, which combination is most likely
options: Domestic rice price falls and domestic production falls
Domestic rice price rises and domestic production rises
Domestic rice price falls and imports rise
questions.explanation: A tariff raises the domestic price relative to the free-trade price. This encourages domestic producers to increase production, although consumers generally face higher prices.

questions.text: A consumer's income is ₦50,000. The prices of X and Y are ₦5,000 and ₦2,500 respectively. If the consumer purchases 6 units of X, the maximum number of units of Y that can be purchased with the remaining income is

If the price of a commodity falls from ₦800 to ₦600 and quantity demanded rises from 2,000 to 2,500 units, using the percentage-change method based on original values, the price elasticity of demand is approximately
questions.explanation: Quantity change = 500/2,000 = 25%. Price change = 200/800 = 25%. PED = 25%/25% = 1.0.

questions.text: A consumer's demand for a commodity increases when the price of a related commodity rises. The cross elasticity of demand between the two commodities is therefore
questions.explanation: When the price of one good rises and demand for the other increases, the goods are substitutes, giving a positive cross elasticity.

questions.text: Which of the following would cause a movement along a demand curve rather than a shift of the curve
options: Change in the commodity's own price
questions.explanation: A change in the commodity's own price causes an extension or contraction along the existing demand curve.

questions.text: If the demand for a commodity is perfectly inelastic, an increase in its price will
options: cause quantity demanded to fall to zero
cause demand to become perfectly elastic
questions.explanation: Perfectly inelastic demand means quantity demanded remains unchanged regardless of price.

questions.text: A government grants fertilizer subsidies to farmers. If fertilizer is a major input in food production, the immediate effect is likely to
options: reduce production costs and increase supply
questions.explanation: The subsidy lowers farmers' effective input costs, encouraging production and shifting food supply outward.

questions.text: A farmer sells 4,000 bags of maize at ₦8,000 per bag. If total production cost is ₦25 million, the farmer's profit is
questions.explanation: Total revenue = 4,000 × ₦8,000 = ₦32 million. Profit = ₦32m − ₦25m = ₦7m.

questions.text: If a producer's total revenue is ₦900,000 and total cost is ₦900,000, the producer is earning
questions.explanation: When total economic revenue equals total economic cost, the firm earns normal profit, meaning economic profit is zero.

questions.text: A firm has total fixed cost of ₦100,000. If output increases from 2,000 units to 4,000 units, average fixed cost will
If marginal cost is greater than average variable cost, average variable cost will
questions.explanation: When MC is above AVC, it pulls the average upward. Therefore AVC rises.

questions.text: A firm operating under perfect competition faces a market price of ₦50. At its current output, MC = ₦50 and ATC = ₦40. The firm is
options: making a loss of ₦10 per unit
making an economic profit of ₦10 per unit
questions.explanation: At profit maximization, P = MC = ₦50. Since ATC = ₦40, profit per unit = ₦50 − ₦40 = ₦10.

questions.text: A perfectly competitive firm should shut down in the short run if
options: price is greater than average variable cost
price falls below average variable cost
total revenue exceeds total variable cost
questions.explanation: If price cannot cover average variable cost, the firm minimizes its loss by temporarily shutting down.

questions.text: Which characteristic most clearly distinguishes monopolistic competition from perfect competition
questions.explanation: Monopolistically competitive firms sell differentiated products, unlike the homogeneous products of perfect competition.

questions.text: An oligopolistic firm's demand is affected by the expected reactions of competitors because
options: there are no barriers to entry
questions.explanation: Strategic interdependence is one of the defining characteristics of oligopoly.

questions.text: A cartel is formed when firms in an industry
options: agree to coordinate their activities, especially output or prices
questions.explanation: A cartel is an agreement among firms to coordinate behaviour, often by restricting output or fixing prices.

questions.text: The major economic danger of a successful cartel is that it may
options: restrict output and charge higher prices
questions.explanation: Cartels attempt to behave like a monopoly by restricting supply and raising prices.

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of land as a factor of production
options: Its supply is fixed in geographical terms
questions.explanation: Land is a natural resource and its total geographical supply is fixed, although its productive use can change.

questions.text: The reward for entrepreneurship is
questions.explanation: The entrepreneur organizes factors of production and bears risk. The reward is profit.

questions.text: The entrepreneur's unique role in production includes
options: making decisions and bearing business risks
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs combine resources, make decisions, innovate and bear business risks.

questions.text: If a worker earns ₦120,000 in occupation A and would earn ₦90,000 in occupation B, the economic rent earned by the worker in A is
questions.explanation: Economic rent = actual earnings − transfer earnings = ₦120,000 − ₦90,000 = ₦30,000.

questions.text: Which of the following would most likely increase the demand for capital
options: Fall in expected profitability of investment
Increase in expected returns from investment
Increase in interest rates with no other change
questions.explanation: Higher expected returns make investment more attractive, increasing the demand for capital.

questions.text: If interest rates rise significantly, investment expenditure is likely to
questions.explanation: Higher interest rates increase the cost of borrowing and can reduce the number of profitable investment projects.

questions.text: A government introduces free primary education mainly because education is considered
options: a merit good with positive external benefits
questions.explanation: Education produces benefits to individuals and society, including productivity and social benefits, making it a merit good.

questions.text: A factory pollutes a nearby river without paying for the damage caused. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Pollution imposes costs on third parties who are not involved in the transaction. This is a negative externality.

questions.text: A government may impose a pollution tax because it aims to
options: encourage firms to ignore environmental costs
make producers take external costs into account
questions.explanation: A pollution tax attempts to internalize the external cost, making firms consider the social cost of pollution.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to be a public good
questions.explanation: National defence is generally non-rival and non-excludable, characteristics of a public good.

questions.text: The free-rider problem arises when
options: people pay more than the cost of a public good
people benefit from a good without contributing to its cost
producers refuse to supply private goods
questions.explanation: People can enjoy certain public goods without directly paying for them, creating the free-rider problem.

questions.text: A government may regulate a natural monopoly because without regulation the monopolist may
options: restrict output and charge excessively high prices
produce at the socially efficient level automatically
questions.explanation: Monopoly power can result in higher prices and lower output than under competitive conditions.

questions.text: If the government sets a price ceiling on rent below the market equilibrium, one likely unintended consequence is
questions.explanation: A binding rent ceiling can discourage supply while increasing demand, producing a shortage of rental housing.

questions.text: A country's population grows from 40 million to 44 million while national income rises from ₦20 trillion to ₦22 trillion. Per capita income will
questions.explanation: Initial per capita income = ₦20tn/40m = ₦500,000. New = ₦22tn/44m = ₦500,000. Therefore it remains unchanged.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains why per capita income may give a misleading picture of living standards
options: It ignores income distribution and non-monetary welfare
It can be calculated from national income
questions.explanation: An average can conceal severe inequality and says little about factors such as health, education and environmental quality.

questions.text: If nominal national income rises by 15% while the price level rises by 20%, real national income will most likely
questions.explanation: Prices increased faster than nominal income, so the purchasing power and real income decreased.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of structural transformation
options: A temporary increase in food prices
Movement of labour from low-productivity agriculture into manufacturing and services
A fall in the exchange rate
questions.explanation: Structural transformation involves a lasting change in the composition of economic activity and employment.

questions.text: A major obstacle to economic development in a low-income country is
questions.explanation: Poor infrastructure, low productivity and inadequate investment can constrain economic development.

questions.text: If the central bank wants to reduce excessive credit creation by commercial banks, it may
questions.explanation: A higher reserve requirement forces banks to keep a larger proportion of deposits as reserves, reducing their capacity to create credit.

questions.text: When the central bank sells government securities in the open market, the likely immediate effect is
questions.explanation: Buyers pay for the securities, withdrawing money from circulation and therefore reducing liquidity.

questions.text: If the money supply increases while the demand for money remains unchanged, the equilibrium interest rate will generally
questions.explanation: An excess supply of money tends to reduce the interest rate, other things being equal.

questions.text: Which of the following is a direct function of money
questions.explanation: Money functions as a medium of exchange, unit of account and store of value, among other functions.

questions.text: If a country's currency depreciates, one likely short-run effect is
options: imports become cheaper in domestic currency
exports become relatively cheaper to foreigners
domestic goods become more expensive abroad
questions.explanation: Depreciation reduces the foreign-currency price of domestic goods, potentially making exports more competitive.

questions.text: A country has exports of $80 billion, imports of $95 billion, and receives $10 billion in net income from abroad. Ignoring other current-account items, its current-account balance is
questions.explanation: Trade balance = $80bn − $95bn = −$15bn. Adding $10bn net income gives −$5bn, therefore a $5 billion deficit.

questions.text: A consumer's income increases from ₦100,000 to ₦120,000, while the quantity of a commodity demanded increases from 40 units to 44 units. The income elasticity of demand, using the original-value method, is
questions.explanation: Percentage change in quantity = 4/40 × 100 = 10%. Percentage change in income = 20/100 × 100 = 20%. Income elasticity = 10/20 = 0.5.

questions.text: If the price of a commodity rises by 15% and its quantity demanded falls by only 5%, the demand for the commodity is
questions.explanation: PED = 5/15 = 0.33. Since elasticity is less than 1, demand is inelastic.

questions.text: A producer discovers that reducing the price of his product by 10% causes total revenue to increase. This indicates that demand for the product is
questions.explanation: When price falls and total revenue rises, quantity demanded must increase proportionately more than the price falls. Therefore demand is elastic.

questions.text: If two goods have a cross elasticity of demand of −2, they are
questions.explanation: A negative cross elasticity indicates that the goods are complements.

questions.text: A consumer's demand for a commodity falls when income rises from ₦80,000 to ₦100,000. The commodity is most likely
questions.explanation: Demand for an inferior good generally falls as income increases.

questions.text: A rightward shift of the supply curve can be caused by
questions.explanation: Lower input prices reduce production costs, encouraging firms to supply more at each price, causing a rightward shift in supply.

questions.text: If both demand and supply increase, the equilibrium
questions.explanation: Both increases in demand and supply cause equilibrium quantity to rise, although the effect on price depends on the relative magnitude of the shifts.

questions.text: A government imposes a tax of ₦50 per unit on producers. If the original equilibrium price was ₦500 and consumers now pay ₦530, the approximate amount of the tax borne by consumers per unit is
questions.explanation: Consumers now pay ₦530 instead of ₦500, so the consumer burden is ₦30 per unit. The remaining ₦20 is borne by producers.

questions.text: A tax imposed on a commodity with highly inelastic demand is likely to
questions.explanation: Consumers are less responsive to price increases when demand is inelastic, so producers can pass a larger proportion of the tax onto consumers.

questions.text: A subsidy to consumers will most directly
questions.explanation: A consumer subsidy reduces the effective cost of purchasing the commodity and therefore increases purchasing power.

questions.text: A firm's total cost rises from ₦700,000 to ₦820,000 when output increases from 10,000 to 12,000 units. Its marginal cost is
questions.explanation: Change in total cost = ₦120,000. Change in output = 2,000. MC = ₦120,000 ÷ 2,000 = ₦60.

questions.text: A firm produces 5,000 units. Its average fixed cost is ₦20 and its average variable cost is ₦50. Its total cost is
If a firm's marginal product of labour is greater than its average product of labour, the average product will
questions.explanation: When marginal product is above average product, it pulls the average upward, causing AP to increase.

questions.text: The law of diminishing returns applies when
options: more units of a variable factor are added to fixed factors
questions.explanation: The law operates in the short run when additional units of a variable factor are combined with fixed factors.

questions.text: A farmer adds more workers to a fixed-size farm. Initially output rises rapidly, but eventually each additional worker adds less to total output. This illustrates
questions.explanation: With land fixed, additional workers eventually contribute smaller increments to output. This is the law of diminishing marginal returns.

questions.text: Which of the following is an external economy of scale
options: Development of specialized suppliers in an industrial cluster
questions.explanation: An external economy benefits firms because the industry or location expands, rather than because of an individual firm's actions.

questions.text: A monopolist maximizes profit at the output where
questions.explanation: The profit-maximizing condition is marginal revenue = marginal cost, provided the relevant second-order condition is satisfied.

questions.text: A monopolist's price is ₦1,000, average total cost is ₦700 and output is 20,000 units. The firm's economic profit is
questions.explanation: Profit per unit = ₦1,000 − ₦700 = ₦300. Total profit = ₦300 × 20,000 = ₦6 million.

questions.text: A monopoly may persist because
options: firms can freely enter the market
there are significant barriers to entry
questions.explanation: Barriers such as patents, legal restrictions, ownership of resources or economies of scale can prevent competitors from entering.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a likely characteristic of monopolistic competition
questions.explanation: Monopolistic competition involves many competing firms, although each has some market power because its product is differentiated.

questions.text: A worker earns ₦200,000 monthly but could earn ₦150,000 in the next-best occupation. His economic rent is
questions.explanation: Economic rent = actual earnings − transfer earnings = ₦200,000 − ₦150,000 = ₦50,000.

questions.text: The demand for labour is described as a derived demand because it depends mainly on
options: demand for the goods and services workers produce
questions.explanation: Firms demand labour because labour helps produce goods and services. Therefore labour demand is derived from product demand.

questions.text: If the marginal revenue product of a worker is greater than the wage paid to the worker, a profit-maximizing firm should generally
questions.explanation: If the additional worker generates more revenue than the wage cost, employing more labour can increase profit.

questions.text: Which of the following would most likely cause an increase in the supply of labour
questions.explanation: Better working conditions can make employment more attractive, increasing labour-force participation and labour supply.

questions.text: If nominal GDP is ₦150 billion and the GDP deflator is 125, real GDP is
questions.explanation: Real GDP = ₦150bn ÷ 1.25 = ₦120bn.

questions.text: Which of the following would increase nominal GDP but not necessarily real GDP
options: A rise in the general price level
An increase in employment at constant prices
questions.explanation: Higher prices increase the money value of output even when actual production has not changed.

questions.text: A country's GDP rises from ₦80 trillion to ₦88 trillion. If prices rise by 5%, the real GDP growth rate is approximately
questions.explanation: Nominal GDP grew by 10%. After allowing for approximately 5% inflation, real growth is about 5%.

questions.text: If population grows faster than real GDP, real GDP per capita will
questions.explanation: When population grows faster than real output, output available per person declines.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to improve the accuracy of GDP estimates in a developing economy
questions.explanation: Improved statistical systems capture previously unrecorded economic activities and produce more reliable estimates.

questions.text: A major limitation of using GDP per capita as a measure of welfare is that it
questions.explanation: GDP per capita is an average and does not reveal how income is distributed among citizens.

questions.text: If the marginal propensity to consume is 0.6, an increase in autonomous investment of ₦20 billion will increase equilibrium income by
questions.explanation: Multiplier = 1/(1 − 0.6) = 2.5. Income increase = ₦20bn × 2.5 = ₦50bn.

questions.text: If the marginal propensity to save is 0.2, the investment multiplier is
questions.explanation: Multiplier = 1/MPS = 1/0.2 = 5.

questions.text: An increase in government spending financed by borrowing is most likely to increase aggregate demand when
options: the economy has substantial unemployed resources
all resources are already fully employed
questions.explanation: When resources are underutilized, increased government spending can stimulate output, employment and aggregate demand.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of expansionary fiscal policy
options: Increasing taxes and reducing government spending
Reducing government spending and increasing interest rates
Increasing government spending and reducing taxes
questions.explanation: Higher government spending and lower taxes increase aggregate demand and are therefore expansionary fiscal measures.

questions.text: During a period of severe inflation caused by excessive demand, the central bank is most likely to
questions.explanation: Higher interest rates discourage borrowing and spending, helping to reduce excessive aggregate demand.

questions.text: If the cash reserve ratio is increased from 10% to 20%, commercial banks' ability to create credit will generally
questions.explanation: Banks must retain a larger proportion of deposits as reserves, leaving less available for lending and credit creation.

questions.text: If the money multiplier is 5 and the monetary base increases by ₦2 billion, the theoretical increase in money supply is
questions.explanation: Money supply increase = multiplier × monetary base increase = 5 × ₦2bn = ₦10bn.

questions.text: If a country's exports are ₦40 billion and imports are ₦55 billion, its visible trade balance is
questions.explanation: Trade balance = exports − imports = ₦40bn − ₦55bn = ₦15bn deficit.

questions.text: A depreciation of the domestic currency is most likely to increase demand for exports because
options: domestic goods become relatively cheaper to foreigners
questions.explanation: Depreciation makes domestic goods cheaper in foreign-currency terms, potentially increasing foreign demand.

questions.text: Country A can produce either 60 tonnes of cocoa or 120 tonnes of rice using the same resources. Country B can produce either 80 tonnes of cocoa or 120 tonnes of rice. Which country has the comparative advantage in cocoa
questions.explanation: For A: 1 cocoa costs 2 rice. For B: 1 cocoa costs 1.5 rice. Country B sacrifices fewer units of rice to produce cocoa, so Country B has the comparative advantage in cocoa.

questions.text: A student has three alternatives after secondary school: attend university, learn a trade, or start a business. If he chooses university, the opportunity cost is
options: the money spent on university fees
the total benefit from university education
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is specifically the next best alternative forgone, not all rejected alternatives.

questions.text: Which of the following best distinguishes positive economics from normative economics
options: Positive economics deals with facts, while normative economics involves value judgments
Positive economics is concerned with consumers only
Normative economics is always based on statistics
Positive economics deals only with government policies
questions.explanation: Positive economics examines what is, while normative economics involves opinions about what ought to be.

questions.text: The mean of five observations is 18. If four of the observations are 12, 15, 20 and 25, the fifth observation is
questions.explanation: Total = 18 × 5 = 90. Known values = 12 + 15 + 20 + 25 = 72. Fifth value = 90 − 72 = 18.

questions.text: A country's economy is described as a mixed economy because
options: both the public and private sectors participate in economic activities
questions.explanation: A mixed economy combines private ownership and market forces with government intervention.

questions.text: A consumer reaches equilibrium under the marginal utility approach when
options: marginal utility of money is zero
marginal utility per naira spent is equal across commodities
prices of all commodities are equal
questions.explanation: Consumer equilibrium occurs when the consumer obtains equal marginal utility per unit of money spent on each commodity.

questions.text: The total utility derived from consuming four units is 50 utils, while total utility from five units is 58 utils. The marginal utility of the fifth unit is
questions.explanation: MU = change in TU = 58 − 50 = 8 utils.

questions.text: A consumer's income remains unchanged but the price of one commodity falls. The budget line will
options: rotate outward from the axis representing the unchanged commodity
questions.explanation: A fall in the price of one commodity increases the maximum quantity of that commodity the consumer can afford, causing the budget line to rotate outward.

questions.text: Consumer surplus is best described as the difference between
options: what a consumer is willing to pay and what the consumer actually pays
questions.explanation: Consumer surplus is the excess of willingness to pay over the actual market price.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of derived demand
options: Demand for labour by a factory
questions.explanation: Labour is demanded because it is used to produce goods and services. Therefore labour demand is derived from product demand.

questions.text: The demand for electricity and the demand for generators may be described as competitive demand when
options: both goods must always be consumed together
one can serve as an alternative to the other for a particular purpose
both goods are produced from the same raw material
questions.explanation: Competitive goods can serve as alternatives in satisfying a particular want.

questions.text: A farmer can produce either 100 tonnes of rice or 50 tonnes of maize with the same resources. Another farmer can produce either 80 tonnes of rice or 60 tonnes of maize. Which farmer has the comparative advantage in maize
questions.explanation: First farmer: 1 maize costs 2 rice. Second farmer: 1 maize costs 80/60 = 1.33 rice. The second farmer sacrifices less rice and therefore has the comparative advantage in maize.

questions.text: A major disadvantage of division of labour is that it may
options: make workers bored due to repetitive tasks
questions.explanation: Excessive specialization may make work monotonous, causing boredom and reduced job satisfaction.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of an external diseconomy
options: Rising congestion and input costs as an entire industrial area expands
Failure of a firm's internal communication system
Wasteful use of machinery by one firm
questions.explanation: External diseconomies arise from factors outside an individual firm, such as congestion and rising industry-wide costs.

questions.text: A producer's total product is 120 units when five workers are employed and 150 units when six workers are employed. The marginal product of the sixth worker is
Which of the following is a characteristic of a cooperative society
options: It is owned exclusively by government
Members jointly own and control it
It is owned by one individual
Its sole objective is political power
questions.explanation: A cooperative is formed by people who voluntarily join together to pursue common economic interests.

questions.text: One major advantage of a limited liability company over a sole proprietorship is that
options: shareholders' liability is generally limited to their investment
questions.explanation: Limited liability protects shareholders from being personally responsible for company debts beyond their agreed investment.

questions.text: A major reason for the existence of a partnership is that it
options: allows two or more persons to combine resources and skills
questions.explanation: Partnerships allow partners to combine capital, expertise and managerial abilities.

questions.text: Privatization involves
options: transferring ownership of a public enterprise to private investors
transferring a private company to government ownership
questions.explanation: Privatization involves transferring ownership/control from the public sector to private ownership.

questions.text: Commercialization of a public enterprise primarily means
options: making it operate more like a profit-oriented business
questions.explanation: Commercialization seeks to make public enterprises more commercially efficient, even where government retains ownership.

questions.text: A country's population grows rapidly while food production grows slowly. One likely consequence is
options: increased dependency and pressure on available resources
questions.explanation: Rapid population growth relative to output can increase resource pressure, unemployment and dependency.

questions.text: The main purpose of a population census is to
options: determine only the country's tax revenue
obtain information about the size and characteristics of the population
questions.explanation: Census data provide information on population size, distribution, age, sex and other characteristics useful for planning.

questions.text: One major problem associated with population census in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: Census exercises may face problems such as undercounting, logistical difficulties and disputes over figures.

questions.text: According to the Malthusian theory, population tends to grow
options: geometrically while food production grows arithmetically
at exactly the same rate as food
questions.explanation: Malthus argued that population tends to grow geometrically, while food supply grows arithmetically, creating potential pressure on resources.

questions.text: A population is considered optimum when
options: it is as large as possible
output per head is maximized given available resources and technology
questions.explanation: Optimum population refers to the population size that produces the highest output per capita under given conditions.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to increase agricultural productivity
questions.explanation: Irrigation and mechanization can improve farm productivity and reduce dependence on rainfall and manual labour.

questions.text: A major cause of instability in farmers' incomes is
options: fluctuations in agricultural prices and output
questions.explanation: Agricultural income is vulnerable to weather conditions, pests, diseases and price fluctuations.

questions.text: Which of the following is a major contribution of agriculture to Nigeria's economy
options: It provides raw materials and employment
questions.explanation: Agriculture provides employment, food, raw materials and export earnings, while supporting industrial activities.

questions.text: Which of the following belongs to the money market rather than the capital market
questions.explanation: The money market deals mainly in short-term financial instruments, such as treasury bills.

questions.text: The primary function of an insurance company is to
questions.explanation: Insurance companies pool risks and provide financial compensation against insured losses.

questions.text: The central bank differs from a commercial bank because the central bank
options: accepts deposits from everyone for ordinary savings
acts as banker to the government and supervises the banking system
exists primarily to maximize private profit
questions.explanation: Central banks perform functions including acting as government banker, bankers' bank and monetary authority.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to increase the money supply through the banking system
options: Sale of securities by the central bank
questions.explanation: A lower reserve requirement gives commercial banks greater capacity to create deposits through lending.

questions.text: A regressive tax is one in which
options: the average tax rate rises as income rises
the average tax burden falls as income rises
everyone pays exactly the same proportion of income
questions.explanation: Under a regressive tax, lower-income earners bear a higher proportion of their income as tax.

questions.text: The principle of certainty in taxation requires that
options: taxpayers should not know when tax is due
the amount, method and time of payment should be clear
tax rates should change every day
questions.explanation: Adam Smith's principle of certainty requires that taxpayers know how much, when and how tax is to be paid.

questions.text: If government expenditure exceeds government revenue in a particular financial year, the government is operating a
questions.explanation: A budget deficit occurs when government expenditure is greater than government revenue.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to be classified as recurrent expenditure
options: Payment of salaries of civil servants
Purchase of a new power plant
questions.explanation: Recurrent expenditure covers regular expenses such as wages, salaries and routine administration.

questions.text: The World Trade Organization primarily deals with
options: international trade rules and trade negotiations
questions.explanation: The WTO provides a framework for international trade rules and negotiations among member countries.

questions.text: The International Monetary Fund is particularly concerned with
options: maintaining international monetary and financial stability
questions.explanation: The IMF promotes international monetary cooperation and financial stability and provides assistance to member countries facing balance-of-payments difficulties.

questions.text: ECOWAS was established primarily to promote
options: economic integration among West African states
questions.explanation: ECOWAS promotes economic cooperation and integration among West African countries.

questions.text: If the Nigerian naira depreciates substantially, which Nigerian group is most likely to benefit, other things being equal
options: Firms heavily dependent on imported inputs
questions.explanation: Depreciation makes Nigerian goods relatively cheaper to foreign buyers, potentially benefiting exporters.

questions.text: A country records a current-account deficit and decides to restrict imports, encourage exports and promote domestic production. The main objective is to
questions.explanation: Restricting excessive imports while encouraging exports can improve the country's balance of payments position.

questions.text: The fundamental economic problem arises because
options: human wants are limited while resources are unlimited
resources are scarce relative to unlimited wants
resources and wants are both unlimited
production is always greater than consumption
questions.explanation: Scarcity exists because available resources are limited in relation to human wants, making choice necessary.

questions.text: A student has ₦10,000 and can either buy a textbook or attend a paid tutorial. He chooses the textbook. If the tutorial would have given him the greatest alternative benefit, the opportunity cost of buying the textbook is
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the next best alternative forgone.

questions.text: Which of the following is a positive economic statement
options: The government should increase teachers' salaries
An increase in taxation reduces disposable income, other things being equal
The minimum wage should be increased
questions.explanation: Positive economics deals with statements that can be tested or verified, rather than value judgments.

questions.text: A point inside a production possibility curve indicates
questions.explanation: A point inside the PPC indicates that some resources are unemployed or inefficiently used.

questions.text: An outward shift of a country's production possibility curve can result from
questions.explanation: Improved technology increases productive capacity and shifts the PPC outward.

questions.text: If a country's resources are used efficiently, a movement from one point to another along its PPC represents
questions.explanation: Movement along the PPC shows the trade-off involved in producing more of one good and less of another.

questions.text: The opportunity cost of producing one additional unit of a commodity is best represented by
questions.explanation: Marginal cost represents the additional cost of producing one more unit, reflecting the relevant opportunity cost.

questions.text: Which economic system relies primarily on the price mechanism to allocate resources
questions.explanation: In a capitalist economy, prices determined largely through demand and supply guide resource allocation.

questions.text: A major weakness of a centrally planned economy is that
options: consumers always have too much choice
bureaucratic decisions may lead to inefficient allocation of resources
questions.explanation: Central planning may suffer from bureaucratic inefficiency and inadequate information about consumers' preferences.

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of a mixed economy
options: Coexistence of private enterprise and government participation
questions.explanation: A mixed economy combines market forces with government intervention.

questions.text: If the price of a commodity increases from ₦500 to ₦600 and quantity supplied rises from 2,000 to 2,500 units, the movement represents
questions.explanation: A rise in the commodity's own price causes an extension along the supply curve.

questions.text: Which of the following will shift the demand curve for a normal good to the right
options: Increase in price of the good itself
questions.explanation: For a normal good, higher income increases demand, shifting the demand curve rightward.

questions.text: If the price of tea rises and consumers consequently demand more coffee, tea and coffee are
questions.explanation: Consumers switch from tea to coffee when tea becomes more expensive, showing that they are substitutes.

questions.text: A fall in the price of a complement will generally
questions.explanation: Cheaper complements make consumption of both goods more attractive, increasing demand for the related good.

questions.text: A commodity whose demand increases by a greater percentage than the increase in income is
questions.explanation: A luxury has an income elasticity greater than one.

questions.text: If price elasticity of demand is zero, demand is
questions.explanation: Perfectly inelastic demand means quantity demanded does not respond to price changes.

questions.text: When demand is unitary elastic, a percentage change in price produces
options: a larger percentage change in quantity demanded
a smaller percentage change in quantity demanded
an equal percentage change in quantity demanded
questions.explanation: Unit elasticity means percentage change in quantity equals percentage change in price.

questions.text: A producer is most likely to bear a larger proportion of an indirect tax when demand for the product is
questions.explanation: When demand is elastic, consumers are more responsive to price increases, making it harder for producers to pass the entire tax onto consumers.

questions.text: A price ceiling becomes effective only when it is set
questions.explanation: A price ceiling below equilibrium prevents the market from reaching its equilibrium price and is therefore binding.

questions.text: A binding price floor normally results in
questions.explanation: A price floor above equilibrium encourages supply while reducing demand, creating a surplus.

questions.text: If total utility continues to increase but at a decreasing rate, marginal utility is
questions.explanation: Total utility rises when marginal utility is positive, but the slower increase means marginal utility is falling.

questions.text: The law of diminishing marginal utility states that
options: total utility must eventually become negative
additional units of a commodity eventually yield smaller increments of utility
price must fall as consumption increases
questions.explanation: As successive units are consumed, the additional satisfaction obtained from each unit generally declines.

questions.text: A consumer maximizes utility when
options: marginal utilities of all goods are zero
marginal utility per unit of money is equal across goods
questions.explanation: Consumer equilibrium occurs when the last naira spent on each commodity provides the same marginal utility.

questions.text: A fall in the price of a commodity can increase its quantity demanded partly because
options: the consumer's real purchasing power rises
the consumer's nominal income necessarily rises
questions.explanation: A lower price increases real income/purchasing power, which is the income effect of a price change.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a factor affecting demand
questions.explanation: Production technology primarily affects supply, not demand.

questions.text: The supply of agricultural products is often relatively inelastic in the short run because
options: agricultural production depends partly on biological and seasonal factors
questions.explanation: Farmers cannot instantly adjust production because of growing periods, weather and biological constraints.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to increase supply
questions.explanation: Better technology can lower production costs and increase productivity, shifting supply rightward.

questions.text: A firm's total revenue is ₦2.4 million from selling 8,000 units. Its average revenue is
If total revenue rises from ₦1,000,000 to ₦1,150,000 when output rises from 10,000 to 12,000 units, marginal revenue is
questions.explanation: MR = change in TR/change in Q = ₦150,000 ÷ 2,000 = ₦75.

questions.text: A firm's total fixed cost is ₦400,000. If output increases from 5,000 to 10,000 units, average fixed cost falls from
Which of the following costs remains unchanged as output changes in the short run
questions.explanation: Fixed costs do not change with output in the short run.

questions.text: A firm has total cost of ₦5 million at 10,000 units and ₦5.8 million at 12,000 units. Its marginal cost over the range is
questions.explanation: Change in TC = ₦800,000. Change in output = 2,000. MC = ₦800,000/2,000 = ₦400.

questions.text: A firm achieves economies of scale when
options: long-run average cost rises as output increases
long-run average cost falls as output increases
total fixed cost increases with every unit
questions.explanation: Economies of scale occur when increasing the scale of production causes long-run average cost to fall.

questions.text: A firm under perfect competition is called a price taker because
options: its individual output is too small to influence market price
questions.explanation: A competitive firm accepts the market price because it has no significant individual influence over market supply.

questions.text: Under perfect competition, the firm's demand curve is
options: perfectly elastic at the market price
questions.explanation: The individual competitive firm can sell any feasible quantity at the prevailing market price, making its demand curve perfectly elastic.

questions.text: A monopolist can maintain abnormal profit in the long run mainly because
options: there are no barriers to entry
entry barriers prevent competitors from entering
questions.explanation: Barriers to entry protect the monopolist from new competitors.

questions.text: Price discrimination occurs when a seller
options: charges different prices to different markets for the same product when cost differences do not justify the difference
charges every consumer the same price
questions.explanation: Price discrimination involves charging different prices based on market or consumer characteristics, not corresponding cost differences.

questions.text: An oligopoly is likely to exhibit price rigidity because
options: firms consider competitors' reactions to price changes
questions.explanation: Oligopolistic firms are interdependent, so a price change may trigger reactions from rivals.

questions.text: The reward for capital as a factor of production is
questions.explanation: The conventional reward for capital is interest.

questions.text: The reward for land is
questions.explanation: The factor reward associated with land is rent.

questions.text: A worker who leaves one job and spends two weeks searching for another job is experiencing
questions.explanation: Frictional unemployment occurs while workers are moving between jobs or searching for suitable employment.

questions.text: Disguised unemployment is most commonly associated with a situation where
options: more workers are employed than are actually required to maintain output
workers lose jobs due to recession
questions.explanation: Disguised unemployment exists when some workers have zero or very low marginal productivity.

questions.text: The demand for labour will increase if
options: demand for the product produced by labour increases
the wage rate rises with no productivity change
questions.explanation: Since labour demand is derived from product demand, higher demand for the product can increase demand for workers.

questions.text: If the marginal revenue product of labour is below the wage rate, a profit-maximizing firm should generally
questions.explanation: If the additional revenue generated by labour is below its cost, reducing employment can increase profit.

questions.text: Economic rent is particularly high for a factor whose supply is
questions.explanation: With perfectly inelastic supply, the entire factor reward can be regarded as economic rent.

questions.text: A major function of an entrepreneur is to
options: coordinate factors and bear business risk
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs combine factors, make decisions, innovate and bear risks.

questions.text: National income is best described as
options: the total money held by citizens
the total income earned by factors of production in an economy over a period
questions.explanation: National income represents the income earned from productive activities by the factors of production.

questions.text: Which of the following is included in GDP
options: Sale of a second-hand car between two individuals
Production of a new car during the current year
questions.explanation: GDP measures the value of newly produced final goods and services within a country during a period.

questions.text: Transfer payments are excluded from GDP because they
options: do not represent payment for current production
questions.explanation: Examples such as pensions and certain welfare payments transfer purchasing power but do not represent current production.

questions.text: If nominal GDP increases while real GDP remains unchanged, the most likely explanation is
options: the general price level has increased
questions.explanation: Nominal GDP can increase solely because of higher prices, even when actual output is unchanged.

questions.text: If nominal GDP is ₦500 billion and the price index is 125, real GDP is
questions.explanation: Real GDP = ₦500bn ÷ 1.25 = ₦400bn.

questions.text: Per capita income is obtained by dividing
questions.explanation: Per capita income measures average income per person: national income ÷ population.

questions.text: A rise in per capita income does not necessarily mean that
questions.explanation: Per capita income is an average and can rise even when some people's incomes fall.

questions.text: Which of the following is a major limitation of GDP as a measure of economic welfare
questions.explanation: GDP does not show how income and output are distributed among citizens.

questions.text: Demand-pull inflation occurs when
options: aggregate demand persistently exceeds productive capacity
questions.explanation: Demand-pull inflation occurs when excess demand puts upward pressure on prices.

questions.text: Cost-push inflation may result from
questions.explanation: Rising wages, fuel prices or raw-material costs can increase production costs and push prices upward.

questions.text: If inflation is 20% and a worker's nominal wage increases by only 10%, the worker's real purchasing power will approximately
questions.explanation: Approximate real wage change = 10% − 20% = −10%.

questions.text: Which group is most likely to suffer from unexpected inflation
questions.explanation: People with fixed incomes lose purchasing power when prices unexpectedly rise.

questions.text: Deflation refers to
options: a persistent fall in the general price level
questions.explanation: Deflation is a sustained decline in the general price level.

questions.text: The Phillips curve traditionally suggests an inverse relationship between
questions.explanation: The traditional short-run Phillips curve depicts an inverse relationship between inflation and unemployment.

questions.text: If MPC = 0.8, the simple expenditure multiplier is
questions.explanation: Multiplier = 1/(1 − MPC) = 1/0.2 = 5.

questions.text: If the marginal propensity to save is 0.25, the multiplier is
questions.explanation: Multiplier = 1/MPS = 1/0.25 = 4.

questions.text: An increase in government expenditure is likely to have the greatest multiplier effect when
questions.explanation: A high MPC means more of each additional income is spent, causing larger rounds of expenditure.

questions.text: Which of the following is an automatic stabilizer
questions.explanation: Progressive taxation automatically reduces disposable income during booms and supports it during downturns, helping to stabilize the economy.

questions.text: Fiscal policy refers mainly to the government's use of
questions.explanation: Fiscal policy involves government decisions concerning taxation, expenditure and borrowing.

questions.text: Monetary policy is primarily concerned with regulating
options: money supply, credit and interest rates
questions.explanation: Monetary policy is used to influence money, credit and interest rates, usually through the central bank.

questions.text: An open-market sale by the central bank tends to
questions.explanation: Selling securities withdraws money from the banking system, reducing liquidity and money supply.

questions.text: An increase in the cash reserve ratio will normally
options: increase excess reserves available for lending
questions.explanation: Banks must keep a larger fraction of deposits as reserves, reducing credit creation.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a function of money
questions.explanation: Money facilitates transactions and valuation, but it does not guarantee profit.

questions.text: A major advantage of money over barter is that money
options: solves the double coincidence of wants problem
questions.explanation: Money allows people to trade without needing each person to want exactly what the other person possesses.

questions.text: Commercial banks create money mainly through
questions.explanation: Deposit creation occurs as banks lend a portion of deposits, subject to reserve requirements and other constraints.

questions.text: The lender of last resort to commercial banks is normally the
questions.explanation: The central bank can provide emergency liquidity to banks facing serious short-term liquidity problems.

questions.text: Which of the following is a direct tax
questions.explanation: Personal income tax is imposed directly on the income of individuals.

questions.text: A major advantage of indirect taxation is that it
options: is relatively easy to collect from transactions
questions.explanation: Indirect taxes such as VAT are collected through transactions and can therefore be relatively convenient to administer.

questions.text: The principle of equity in taxation implies that
options: every taxpayer must pay exactly the same amount
taxpayers should contribute according to their ability to pay
questions.explanation: Equity requires a tax system to distribute the burden fairly, often according to ability to pay.

questions.text: A government budget surplus occurs when
questions.explanation: A surplus occurs when government revenue is greater than expenditure.

questions.text: Which of the following is capital expenditure
questions.explanation: Capital expenditure creates or improves long-term productive assets.

questions.text: Public debt can become problematic when
options: debt-service obligations become excessively large relative to government revenue
debt is used for productive investment
questions.explanation: Excessive debt servicing can place pressure on government finances and crowd out other expenditure.

questions.text: The balance of trade is the difference between
questions.explanation: Balance of trade refers specifically to the difference between exports and imports of goods.

questions.text: A country has visible exports of $80 million and visible imports of $100 million. Its balance of trade is
questions.explanation: $80m − $100m = −$20m, meaning a $20 million deficit.

questions.text: A persistent balance-of-payments deficit may put downward pressure on a country's currency because
options: demand for foreign currency may exceed its supply
domestic prices must fall to zero
questions.explanation: Heavy demand for foreign currency to finance imports and other payments can put depreciation pressure on the domestic currency.

questions.text: A depreciation of a country's currency can improve its trade balance if
options: exports and imports are sufficiently responsive to price changes
exports become more expensive to foreigners
questions.explanation: If demand responds sufficiently to changed relative prices, depreciation can increase exports and reduce imports—the condition underlying the Marshall-Lerner approach.

questions.text: Comparative advantage is determined primarily by
questions.explanation: Comparative advantage arises when a producer can produce a good at a lower opportunity cost than another producer.

questions.text: International trade can benefit countries because it
options: allows specialization based on comparative advantage
questions.explanation: Countries can specialize and trade, potentially increasing total production and consumption possibilities.

questions.text: A tariff is
questions.explanation: A tariff is a tax imposed on imported goods.

questions.text: An import quota differs from a tariff because a quota
options: directly specifies a maximum quantity of imports
questions.explanation: A quota is a quantitative restriction on the amount of a good that may be imported.

questions.text: One argument for protectionism is that it may
options: expose infant industries to unlimited foreign competition
guarantee lower prices in every case
questions.explanation: The infant-industry argument says temporary protection can help new domestic firms develop before facing full foreign competition.

questions.text: ECOWAS was established to promote
questions.explanation: ECOWAS seeks to deepen economic cooperation and integration in West Africa.

questions.text: The IMF is more directly associated with
options: international monetary cooperation and balance-of-payments assistance
questions.explanation: The IMF provides financial and policy support related to external imbalances and monetary stability.

questions.text: The World Bank primarily provides
questions.explanation: The World Bank supports long-term development projects and poverty-reduction efforts.

questions.text: Economic development differs from economic growth because development
options: refers only to an increase in population
includes broader improvements in welfare and structural conditions
questions.explanation: Growth mainly refers to an increase in output, while development includes structural, social and welfare improvements.

questions.text: Which of the following is a social indicator of development
questions.explanation: Life expectancy measures an important aspect of health and human welfare.

questions.text: A country with high GDP but poor healthcare, education and severe inequality may have
options: high economic growth but weaker overall development
questions.explanation: High output alone does not guarantee improvements in human welfare and distribution.

questions.text: Human capital formation involves
options: investment in people's education, skills and health
questions.explanation: Education, training and healthcare improve workers' skills and productive capacity.

questions.text: A major obstacle to economic development in many developing countries is
options: low productivity and inadequate capital formation
questions.explanation: Low productivity and insufficient investment can restrict economic transformation and growth.

questions.text: If a country increases agricultural productivity through irrigation, improved seeds and mechanization, one likely long-run effect is
questions.explanation: Higher agricultural productivity can increase food availability and contribute to food security.

questions.text: One major reason agricultural supply may be unstable is
options: agricultural output is completely independent of weather
farmers face climatic and biological uncertainties
questions.explanation: Weather, pests, diseases and other biological factors can cause substantial variations in agricultural output.

questions.text: The main reason for providing agricultural extension services is to
options: prevent farmers from using modern methods
transfer improved farming knowledge and techniques to farmers
questions.explanation: Extension officers help farmers adopt improved technologies, production methods and management practices.

questions.text: If a country has abundant labour but scarce capital, which production technique is generally more appropriate, other things being equal
questions.explanation: A labour-abundant, capital-scarce economy can often make more efficient use of its resources through labour-intensive production.

questions.text: A country experiences rapid economic growth, but most of the increase in output comes from extracting a finite natural resource while investment in education and infrastructure remains low. The greatest concern is that
options: growth may not be sustainable in the long run
questions.explanation: Dependence on a finite resource without sufficient diversification and human-capital investment can produce growth that is unsustainable and vulnerable to future shocks.
